plates.side_label: 1852 HELMHOLTZ RGB METAMERS (RED 630 NM + GREEN 530 NM = 580 NM YELLOW) & 1995 DALTON DNA (MISSING 534 NM M-CONE GENE)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked RGB screen metamers and Dalton X-chromosome DNA chart from Helmholtz (1852), Nathans (1986 Science 232: 193–202), and Hunt & Mollon (17 February 1995 Science 267: 984–988) shows how 580 nm monochromatic yellow light and a 630 nm Red + 530 nm Green LED pair produce identical L/M cone excitation ratios (~150,000 cones/mm² in the fovea), and how Dalton's X chromosome carried the L-cone (red) gene but lacked the M-cone (green) gene.

teach_overlay.label: RGB METAMERS & 17 FEB 1995 DALTON DNA: 150,000 CONES/MM² IN FOVEA · MISSING 534 NM M-CONE GENE (DEUTERANOPIA)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked RGB screen metamers & Dalton X-chromosome DNA chart on period paper from Helmholtz (1852), Nathans (1986 Science 232: 193–202), and Hunt & Mollon (17 February 1995 Science 267: 984–988) showing how 580 nm monochromatic yellow light and a 630 nm Red + 530 nm Green LED pair produce identical L/M cone excitation ratios, and how Dalton's X chromosome carried the L-cone (red) gene but lacked the M-cone (green) gene
teach_overlay.scale: a single square millimetre at the centre of your retina packs roughly one hundred and fifty thousand cone cells — yet every colour you have ever seen is mixed from just three cone types
